relationships.subject: MrgprB2
relationships.evidence_quote: Compared to C57BL/6J mice, MrgprB2−/− female or male mice could significantly alleviate cisplatin-induced cold allodynia (Fig. 1F and 1I).

relationships.subject: MrgprB2
relationships.evidence_quote: However, the tryptase expression in hindpaw tissues (Fig. 2H-J) or DRGs (Fig. 2 K-M) was not increased in MrgprB2-/- mice after modeling.

relationships.subject: tryptase
relationships.evidence_quote: Additionally, blocking tryptase with APC366 could significantly reduce the cold allodynia and thermal hypersensitivity induced by cisplatin

relationships.subject: MrgprB2
relationships.evidence_quote: Moreover, there were no change of PAR2 expression in MrgprB2-/- mice after modeling (Fig. 3H-J).

relationships.subject: FSLLRY-NH2
relationships.evidence_quote: In addition, blocking PAR2 receptor with FSLLRY-NH2 significantly alleviated cisplatin-induced pain (Fig. 3E-G).

relationships.subject: PAR2
relationships.evidence_quote: Additionally, we observed MrgprD mRNA expression was decreased in isolated DRG neurons induced by SLIGRL-NH2 stimulation (Fig. S5A), indicating the negative regulatory effect of PAR2 on MrgprD.

relationships.subject: substance P
relationships.evidence_quote: Therefore, we suggested that MrgprB2 might be activated by substance P to recruit inflammatory cells and participate in cisplatin-induced pain.

key_findings: MrgprB2/tryptase/PAR2 axis drives cisplatin-induced pain: MrgprB2 knockout prevents tryptase and PAR2 upregulation and reduces allodynia.
PAR2 negatively regulates MrgprD expression in DRG (indirectly, no direct interaction by Co-IP), and PAR2 inhibition blocks cisplatin-induced MrgprD downregulation, linked to later-stage pain relief.
